summary: Citizens of the EU, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, most of Latin America and a long list of other countries enter Uruguay visa-free for up to 90 days, and the stay can be extended with the Dirección Nacional de Migración; other nationalities need a visa from a Uruguayan consulate.

CN.notes: Uruguay's Ministry of the Interior says holders of an ordinary Chinese passport with a valid US, Canadian, UK or EU visa can enter without a Uruguayan consular visa, provided their first entry is through Carrasco, Montevideo, Colonia or Laguna del Sauce.

quote.text: Portadores de pasaporte común de República Popular China con visa vigente de EE.UU., Canadá, Reino Unido o UE pueden ingresar sin visa consular uruguaya siempre que el primer ingreso sea por Carrasco, Montevideo, Colonia o Laguna del Sauce.

DO.notes: Uruguay's Ministry of the Interior says holders of an ordinary Dominican Republic passport with a US or UK visa valid for at least 6 months can enter without a stamped consular visa.

quote.text: Portadores de pasaporte común de República Dominicana con visa de EE.UU. o Reino Unido vigente por al menos 6 meses pueden ingresar sin visa consular estampada.

fee.notes: 3 consular pesos (USD 42), charged only if the visa is granted; official and diplomatic passports pay nothing. The Foreign Ministry says consular fees change on 1 January each year.

source.name: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores — Inicio de solicitud de visas (gub.uy)

fee.notes: 3 consular pesos (USD 42), the visa fee the Foreign Ministry publishes, charged only if the visa is granted. The application asks for an invitation letter or hotel booking and proof of funds.

source.name: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores — Inicio de solicitud de visas (gub.uy)

passportValidity.text: The UK government says your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay and have at least one blank page for an entry stamp. Visa applicants need a passport valid for at least 6 months after arrival in Uruguay, according to the Foreign Ministry.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: The US CDC says Uruguay does not require yellow fever vaccination for entry.

source.name: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Uruguay traveler health

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for Uruguay; the Foreign Ministry's visa requirements do not include insurance.

source.name: Gobierno de Uruguay — Inicio de solicitud de visas (MRREE visa application procedure) (requirements: no travel insurance listed)

onwardTicket.text: Visa applicants must present a travel booking (reserva de viaje) with the application, according to the Foreign Ministry. No official source we could read states a ticket requirement for visa-exempt visitors.

source.name: Gobierno de Uruguay — Inicio de solicitud de visas (MRREE visa application procedure)

proofOfFunds.text: Visa applicants must show proof of economic solvency with the application, according to the Foreign Ministry. No official source we could read publishes an amount, or a funds requirement for visa-exempt visitors.

source.name: Gobierno de Uruguay — Inicio de solicitud de visas (MRREE visa application procedure)

currencyLimits.text: Cash, precious metals or other monetary instruments worth USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared to customs on entry and exit.

source.name: Dirección Nacional de Aduanas, Uruguay — Normativa vigente para transporte de valores

notes: The UK government's travel advice says it is illegal for visitors to import fruit, vegetables, animals or dairy products and their derivatives, flammable materials, alkaloids, narcotics or obscene objects, and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

safety.text: The UK government says street crime happens in Montevideo, including mugging and robbery (sometimes armed), that criminals regularly break into cars left on the street, and that crime rates are generally lower in other parts of Uruguay. The Government of Canada advises a high degree of caution in Montevideo due to crime and says petty crime, muggings and armed robbery are more common in places including the Ciudad Vieja.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Uruguay?
faq.answer: Uruguay waives visas for a broad list of nationalities — including the EU, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel, Russia and most of Latin America and the Caribbean — for tourist stays of up to 90 days. Everyone else applies for a visa at a Uruguayan consulate.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Uruguay without a visa?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days for visa-free tourist stays. The Dirección Nacional de Migración can extend the stay (prórroga); the request must be made at least 15 days before the permitted stay runs out.

faq.question: Can I enter Uruguay with a national ID card instead of a passport?
faq.answer: No official source we could read lists which national identity cards Uruguay accepts instead of a passport. The Dirección Nacional de Migración accepts a national identity document or a passport when you apply to extend a stay.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Uruguay?
faq.answer: No. United States passport holders enter visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days, and the stay can be extended with the Dirección Nacional de Migración.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Uruguay?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply to the Dirección Nacional de Migración at least 15 days before your permitted stay runs out, with your passport or national identity document. The fee is 225.60 indexed units (UI) while your stay is still valid, or 345 UI once it has expired.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Uruguay?
faq.answer: No. The US CDC says Uruguay does not require yellow fever vaccination for entry.
